title: CoreWeave enters India with 240 MW AI data centre in Navi Mumbai
excerpt: CoreWeave will lease 240 MW at AdaniConneX's Navi Mumbai campus, with Nvidia Vera Rubin chips from mid-2028. What it means for India's AI compute race.
content:
CoreWeave, the Nasdaq-listed company that rents out Nvidia GPU computing to AI labs, is entering India with 240 megawatts (MW) of data centre capacity at AdaniConneX's Taloja campus in Navi Mumbai, it announced on 6 October 2026. The first phase is due in mid-2028, and CoreWeave will also open an office in India and hire locally.

CoreWeave did not say how much it will spend. Bloomberg reported that the investment will run to multiple billions of dollars over the life of the project, according to The Next Web and Mint. Mint and Bloomberg describe them as CoreWeave's first data centres in India.

Key takeaways

  • CoreWeave will be the only tenant of three 80 MW buildings at AdaniConneX's Taloja campus, with an option to add up to another 240 MW there (CoreWeave).
  • It plans to run Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform for AI training, inference and agent workloads. The first phase is expected in mid-2028.
  • India has about 2.2 GW of operating data centre capacity, built over three decades. Wood Mackenzie expects 12 GW by 2030, with AI-specific capacity rising nearly 24 times to 6.5 GW, Mint reported.
  • For Indian AI startups, nothing changes before 2028. The deal matters more as a sign of where large-scale GPU capacity will sit later this decade.

What CoreWeave and AdaniConneX announced

The release, datelined Livingston, New Jersey and Mumbai, sets out the main terms. The campus will be three 80 MW buildings designed for dense AI hardware, with direct liquid cooling for the GPU halls and a non-evaporative chilled water system, meaning the cooling does not depend on evaporating water. Capacity will come online in phases after the first one in mid-2028 (CoreWeave).

"India has the talent, developers, and ambition to become a major center of AI innovation," said Sachin Jain, CoreWeave's chief operating officer, in the announcement. CoreWeave also said the investment supports the IndiaAI Mission, the government's programme to build national AI computing capacity.

AdaniConneX is a 50:50 joint venture between Adani Enterprises and the US data centre operator EdgeConneX. It was set up with a goal of building a 1 GW data centre platform in India, according to the boilerplate in CoreWeave's release. Inc42 reported the deal on 8 October as CoreWeave's India entry.

Who CoreWeave is

CoreWeave was founded in 2017 and listed on Nasdaq in March 2025. It builds and leases GPU clusters to AI developers and large companies. It had about 4.2 gigawatts of contracted power as of its 11 August 2026 earnings call, the company says.

The business is large and still loss-making. For the quarter to June 2026, CoreWeave reported revenue of $2.58 billion, up from $1.21 billion a year earlier, and a net loss of about $626 million. Its revenue backlog stood at $104 billion, Pulse 2.0 reported from the results. Chief executive Mike Intrator said in September the company was "largely sold out" of capacity, according to Mint.

India is CoreWeave's second Asia-Pacific market. In August it announced three data centres in Indonesia with 360 MW of contracted power, its first in the region, Reuters reported. At the time it said customers in Asia increasingly need AI computing close to their data and users, for speed and for data-location reasons. The same report said CoreWeave ran 49 data centres worldwide and planned $31 billion to $35 billion of capital spending in 2026.

Why Navi Mumbai, and why Adani

The CoreWeave deal sits inside a much larger Adani bet. In February 2026, the Adani Group said it would invest $100 billion by 2035 in renewable-powered data centres for AI, taking AdaniConneX's capacity from 2 GW to 5 GW, Outlook Business reported. The plan is backed by the group's Khavda renewable energy project in Gujarat.

AdaniConneX is already the partner on Google's largest India project. In October 2025, Google said it would invest about $15 billion from 2026 to 2030 in an AI hub in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, with AdaniConneX and Airtel as partners (Google). That project has been cleared for 2.51 GW, The Next Web reported. Adani has also said it works with Microsoft on projects in Hyderabad and Pune.

With CoreWeave, AdaniConneX now counts both Google and CoreWeave as partners on large AI projects. A committed tenant matters because a data centre built for AI is expensive to fill on speculation. A single tenant taking all three buildings, with an option on more, lowers the risk for the developer.

How big is 240 MW?

Data centres are measured by the electrical power they can draw, because power limits how many GPUs can run. India's whole installed base is about 2.2 GW, built up over three decades, according to Wood Mackenzie figures cited by Mint and Investing.com. CoreWeave's 240 MW alone equals roughly a tenth of that installed base, and the full 480 MW option about a fifth.

It will not be the only large project. Amazon, Microsoft and Google have together pledged nearly $57 billion for cloud infrastructure in India, and Meta is working with Reliance Industries on an AI-focused data centre, its first in the country, Mint reported. Wood Mackenzie expects AI-specific capacity to grow nearly 24-fold to 6.5 GW by 2030.

What it means for Indian AI startups

  • Not yet. The first capacity is due in mid-2028. Startups that need GPUs today will still rely on existing clouds, IndiaAI Mission compute and overseas regions.
  • Local frontier hardware, later. If the timeline holds, Indian companies will be able to rent Nvidia's newest systems from a provider in India, which helps with speed for users and with keeping data in the country.
  • Jobs. CoreWeave says it will set up an Indian office and hire locally. We list roles only from official career pages; see our AI and ML jobs board and all jobs.
  • Pricing pressure. More GPU suppliers in one market generally means more choice for buyers. How CoreWeave prices capacity in India has not been disclosed.

What we do not know yet

CoreWeave has not disclosed the investment amount, the lease terms with AdaniConneX, any named Indian customers, or how many GPUs the site will hold. The "multiple billions" figure comes from Bloomberg's reporting, not from the company. We have left out any estimate of GPU count or cost for that reason.

Bottom line

CoreWeave's move turns India from a market served from abroad into a place where one of the biggest AI clouds will own capacity, and it confirms AdaniConneX as the default partner for foreign AI infrastructure here. The deal is long-dated, so its real test is whether the buildings, the power and the Vera Rubin chips arrive on schedule in 2028. Follow India's AI infrastructure deals on our news page and funding tracker.

FAQ

Where is CoreWeave's India data centre?

At AdaniConneX's Taloja campus in Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra, across three 80 MW buildings.

When will it open?

The first phase is expected in mid-2028, with more capacity in phases after that.

How much is CoreWeave investing in India?

CoreWeave has not given a figure. Bloomberg reported the investment will total multiple billions of dollars over the life of the project.

What is AdaniConneX?

A 50:50 joint venture between Adani Enterprises and EdgeConneX that builds data centres in India. It is also Google's partner on the Visakhapatnam AI hub.

Will CoreWeave hire in India?

Yes. It says it will open an office in India and hire locally. Roles had not been detailed at the time of writing.
